ai.title: README.md: Replace AGI-level with AI
ai.summary: Updated the introductory description in `npm-app/README.md` to remove the 'AGI-level' claim, replacing it with 'AI coding assistant'. This change aligns the documentation with the project's actual capabilities and avoids overstating the technology. The modification is limited to the `npm-app` package README.

eli5.text: The project's description stopped calling itself a super-advanced, near-human-level coding helper and is now accurately described as an AI coding assistant that runs from your command line. If you read the project's homepage text, you'd notice it no longer makes the grand claim about being 'AGI-level' and instead uses the more down-to-earth term 'AI'. This is a small wording change in the project's intro text, and it's live now since the documentation has been updated.

ai.title: Add MAXITERATIONS guard to mainPrompt loop
ai.summary: Added `iterationCount` and `MAX_ITERATIONS = 20` to the `while (!isComplete)` loop in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`. Prevents infinite loops by forcing exit after 20 iterations. Logs 'Reached maximum number of iterations in mainPrompt' via `console.log` and `debugLog` if cap hit.

eli5.text: The program now has a safety limit so it stops trying to solve a problem after most 20 attempts instead of looping forever. If that limit kicks in, the system logs a message saying it gave up. This is purely a behind-the-scenes reliability fix and is live today; you won't notice any new features, but the program is less likely to hang silently.

ai.title: Remove stream error catch and lower max iterations
ai.summary: Removed try/catch wrapper from processStreamWithFiles in backend/src/process-stream.ts and reduced MAX_ITERATIONS from 20 to 10 in backend/src/main-prompt.ts. This prevents silent failures that previously resulted in empty continuation messages when stream errors occurred. Scope covers backend stream processing and prompt iteration logic.

eli5.text: The system will now stop trying to fix streaming problems by catching and hiding errors internally; instead, when a streaming error happens, it will surface properly rather than silently producing empty follow-up messages. Additionally, the maximum number of processing iterations has been reduced from 20 to 10, which prevents the system from potentially looping indefinitely but also means it will stop sooner if it hits repetitive issues. If you were using the system and it started acting oddly during file processing or seemed to stall, those behaviors should now be more visible and predictable.

ai.title: Increase deploy.sh boot disk size to 20GB
ai.summary: backend/deploy.sh GCE instance creation now sets --boot-disk-size=20GB, up from 10GB. Change addresses storage space constraints for container mount /app/logs and host path /var/log/app. Scope limited to backend deploy script; no impact on runtime code or model configurations.

eli5.text: When the backend deployment script sets up a new server on Google Cloud, it now allocates a 20GB boot disk instead of a 10GB one. This only affects backend deployments that use the deploy script and does not change any runtime code or model configurations. The extra storage space addresses storage space constraints for the container mount /app/logs and host path /var/log/app, so you would notice more available disk space when checking the server. This change is live today.

ai.title: Deploy script prunes Docker images and uses timestamp tags
ai.summary: backend/deploy.sh now runs docker system prune -af --volumes on the VM before deployment to clear old images. Container references switch from :latest to :$TIMESTAMP for both create and update paths. Boot disk size reverts to 10GB on new instances. Internal deploy tooling only.

eli5.text: When a new version of the assistant is deployed to a live server, the system now automatically clears out old versions that were sitting around from previous deployments, freeing up disk space before the fresh copy is installed. Each deployed version is now tagged with a unique timestamp instead of just calling it 'latest', so you can always tell exactly which version you're running and roll back if needed. New servers are created with a smaller 10GB startup disk again (down from a temporary 20GB bump), matching the original size. Only people managing the deployment tooling will notice these changes; the assistant itself behaves exactly as before.
